subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Should agent-visible WebChat client type be exposed as trusted Gateway-attested metadata, as an explicitly untrusted client hint, or not exposed to agents?
rationale: Current source already has connect-time client metadata, but exposing it to agents can affect native-only behavior, diagnostics, or privileged UX, so automation should not choose the trust semantics or carrier shape.

options.title: Gateway-attested metadata
options.body: Propagate validated `connect.client` identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document exactly what agents may trust.

options.title: Untrusted diagnostic hint
options.body: Expose only a clearly labeled untrusted hint for debugging and forbid agents from treating it as a capability or permission signal.

options.title: Decline runtime exposure
options.body: Keep client identity limited to Gateway diagnostics until there is a stronger client-attestation design.

recommendation.title: Gateway-attested metadata
recommendation.body: Propagate validated `connect.client` identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document exactly what agents may trust.

likelyOwner.reason: The Gateway protocol/client metadata boundary is the central decision point and PR history points to this owner for that surface.
